scenarios.description: Invoice phishing followed by session reuse. All telemetry is simulated for training.

response_plan.basis: Shared domain response procedure extracted from the supplied playbook.
response_plan.priority_guidance: Start at P2 for confirmed mailbox compromise. Declare P1 for active material payment diversion, privileged access or confirmed sensitive disclosure.
response_plan.response_lead: SOC L2 with identity and email administrators
response_plan.response_assumption: Treat fin01 and session s101 as compromised while investigating the mailbox, endpoint and payment exposure. The sample supports unauthorized access; external delivery of forwarded content remains unverified.

steps: SOC L1 verifies the user report through a known contact and preserves the original message, complete headers, message ID and reported click time.
SOC L1 records fin01, LT-FIN01, s101 and the mailbox identifiers. Keep event time, report time and source time zone separate.
SOC L1 links message m001, the proxy visit and subsequent authenticated actions. A delivered email alone does not establish compromise.
SOC L1 confirms the unfamiliar session performed mailbox reads or created r01. Check whether the user recognizes those exact actions.
Finance checks affected invoice conversations and pending beneficiary changes immediately. Hold suspicious unreleased instructions under the approved fraud procedure.
SOC L1 escalates with the evidence IDs, current impact, requested identity control and missing delivery audit. Preserve short retention logs first.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: SOC L2 opens one incident for the campaign and appoints the identity and email owners. Link endpoint and fraud investigations to that record.
The incident commander sets priority from actual access, privilege, disclosure and payment state. Record why a later priority change occurs.
The response lead establishes a trusted contact channel and assigns collection, containment and business verification owners with decision times.

Privacy and legal assess exposed message content and notification applicability. Communications prepares a factual update without distributing the phishing content broadly. Authorized activity to test CHG001 is a legitimate retention change on a different mailbox; it does not explain r01.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: SOC L2 reconstructs m001 delivery, URL access, s101 authentication, 74 read observations and rule r01 creation using stable identifiers.
The identity team checks token issuance, authentication methods, device registrations, unusual factor changes and sessions active before and after the alert.
The email team exports rule history, forwarding settings, delegated access, sends, mailbox reads and message trace for the complete available interval.
The email team hunts the sender, reply address, destination and rule target across all recipients. Separate delivered, clicked and compromised populations.
Endpoint response examines browser activity, process ancestry and persistence on LT-FIN01. Request DFIR when credential theft or execution needs deeper acquisition.
Finance compares changed banking instructions with the vendor register and independent callbacks. Record queued, released, settled and recalled payments separately.
SOC L2 tests CHG001 against its mailbox, purpose and time. A retention change on another mailbox does not authorize r01.
Privacy scopes unique messages and recipients using delivery evidence. Record unknown disclosure where read counts or forwarding configuration cannot prove delivery.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The identity administrator restricts fin01, revokes relevant identity sessions and coordinates application session termination. Verify old mailbox access is denied.
The email administrator preserves and disables r01 and other unauthorized forwarding. Confirm no equivalent rule, delegate or application grant remains active.
The email administrator preserves original messages and promptly quarantines matching copies. Block confirmed destinations with a scope and expiry that preserve legitimate supplier communications.
Endpoint response isolates an affected endpoint when execution or credential theft is supported. Keep the approved response channel and preserve volatile evidence when feasible.
Finance maintains payment holds or starts recall through established bank contacts. Obtain acknowledgement and actual settlement state instead of relying on an email request.
SOC L2 searches for postcontainment mailbox and token activity. Escalate surviving sessions or new rules as evidence of an incomplete control. 01 Eradication recovery and closure
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The identity owner resets exposed credentials from a trusted device and removes unauthorized authentication methods, device registrations and grants after preserving evidence.
Endpoint response rebuilds compromised devices when execution scope is uncertain. Correct the proven theft or execution path before returning the account.
The email owner removes unauthorized delegation and forwarding, reviews mail authentication controls and preserves the removed configuration in the incident record.
Finance repairs verified vendor details with dual approval and independent callback. Detection engineering adds tested session and rule correlations with approved exceptions.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The identity owner demonstrates denial of old access and successful clean sign in with the approved authentication method. Save the resource level test result.
The email owner tests normal invoice receipt and reply while unauthorized external forwarding remains blocked. Confirm audit delivery and rule visibility.
Finance reconciles affected instructions, actual settlements and recall outcomes. The business owner approves resumption of the payment workflow.
SOC L2 monitors related identities, grants and rules for an approved period; this exercise starts with 48 hours and extends for evidence gaps.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: SOC L2 records confirmed mailbox access, the bounded message scope and unknown forwarding delivery. Cite evidence rather than calling all recipients compromised.
The response lead records the entry path, failed session or forwarding controls and proof that each corrective action works.
Privacy and finance record notification decisions, customer effects and financial outcome. Assign outstanding provider evidence and residual risk to named owners.
The incident owner obtains business acceptance and schedules a safe repeat test of the lure, session denial and payment verification controls.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

scenario_notes.text: Obtain outbound forwarding delivery logs and the full mailbox audit interval to assess disclosure.

scenario_notes.label: Validate approved activity
scenario_notes.text: CHG001 is a legitimate retention change on a different mailbox; it does not explain r01.

response_plan.disclaimer: Training guidance based on the supplied playbook. Validate decisions against your organization’s incident response plan, service ownership, legal duties, and change authority before real-world use.

tool_workflow.label: Cross-tool investigation and resolution
tool_workflow.training_note: Simulated analyst workflow, not a live integration. Product menus, telemetry and response permissions depend on the licensed product version and tenant configuration.
tool_workflow.incident_focus: Phishing and business email compromise: Invoice phishing followed by session reuse. Establish confirmed scope, business impact, initial access, affected identities/assets and evidence gaps before selecting disruptive actions.

tools.name: Proofpoint
tools.role: Email security and initial-delivery evidence
tools.investigate: message delivery, sender authentication, URL/attachment verdicts, clicks and recipient scope. Preserve message ID, headers, verdicts, recipients, URLs and attachment hashes where available.
tools.actions: Quarantine/purge only confirmed malicious messages through approved mail-security workflows. Search for campaign-wide recipients and post-delivery exposure.
tools.when_not_applicable: If there is no supported email vector or relevant telemetry, document why Proofpoint is not implicated instead of inventing a finding.

tools.name: CrowdStrike Falcon
tools.role: Endpoint detection, execution and host scope
tools.investigate: endpoint process ancestry, browser/Office activity, downloads and detections around click time. Pivot by host/device ID, user, process tree, file hash and UTC event time.
tools.actions: Use approved host containment/remediation only when evidence and incident authority justify it. Record detection/host IDs and action results.
tools.when_not_applicable: If no endpoint is implicated or telemetry is unavailable, document the gap and continue with other relevant sources.

tools.name: ExtraHop
tools.role: Network detection, movement and egress correlation
tools.investigate: DNS, external destinations, suspicious egress and mailbox/endpoint-related network activity. Pivot by source/destination, DNS, protocol, device and UTC time window.
tools.actions: Preserve alert/record identifiers and distinguish observed traffic from inferred intent. Escalate missing visibility as an evidence gap.
tools.when_not_applicable: No observed traffic is not proof of no activity. Record sensor coverage and seek approved alternate telemetry.

tools.name: ServiceNow
tools.role: Incident record, coordination and audit trail
tools.investigate: Create/link the incident and correlate findings from Proofpoint, Falcon and ExtraHop using stable IDs and timestamps. Maintain one authoritative timeline.
tools.actions: Track severity rationale, affected assets/CIs, evidence links, task owners, approvals, communications, containment results, recovery tests and closure sign-off.
tools.when_not_applicable: If ServiceNow is unavailable in the exercise, use a clearly labeled mock ticket rather than implying a real ticket exists.

tool_workflow.correlation_keys: Scenario ID, UTC timestamps, user/principal, host/device ID, source/destination IP, DNS/domain, message ID, URL/file hash, process/detection ID, API/request/session ID where relevant, affected asset/CI and ServiceNow incident number. Use only identifiers relevant to this scenario.
tool_workflow.scenario_specific_check: Preserve prompt/run/tool-call traces with access controls. Test mitigations with safe replay and do not grant agents extra privileges during investigation.
tool_workflow.containment_plan: Quarantine confirmed malicious mail; revoke compromised sessions and address mailbox rules through approved identity/mail workflows.
service_now_fields: Short description with scenario ID and confirmed incident type
Severity and rationale tied to business impact
Affected user, endpoint, application, service or configuration item (CI)
UTC timeline and stable evidence identifiers
Proofpoint, Falcon and ExtraHop findings with evidence links/export references
Facts, hypotheses and evidence gaps clearly separated
Containment/eradication task, owner, approval, timestamp and result
Business impact and privacy/legal/operations escalation where relevant
Recovery tests, residual risk, closure reason and lessons learned
tool_workflow.success_criteria: Verify at the affected resource that the malicious action/access path no longer succeeds, the original cause is addressed, business service functions normally, monitoring shows no recurrence in a defined observation window, and evidence plus residual risks are recorded.
safety_guardrails: Start with read-only investigation where feasible and preserve original evidence and timestamps.
Obtain incident-command, system-owner and change approvals before disruptive actions.
Do not claim a product action succeeded unless its result is recorded and independently verified.
Do not paste passwords, tokens, private keys or unnecessary customer/employee data into ServiceNow.
All timeline events are synthetic training data. Do not execute response actions against production systems.

response_plan.basis: Scenario-specific response adaptations from the supplied playbook, combined with domain activation guidance and generalized industry-practice closure steps.
response_plan.response_lead: Incident commander with finance and fraud teams

steps: Call the supplier using a number from the approved vendor register, independent of the email. Ask finance whether settlement has actually occurred. Treat imminent material payment diversion as P1 even while the origin of the fraudulent email remains uncertain.
phases.source_basis: Scenario-specific response adaptation in the supplied playbook

steps: SOC L2 opens one incident for the campaign and appoints the identity and email owners. Link endpoint and fraud investigations to that record.
The incident commander sets priority from actual access, privilege, disclosure and payment state. Record why a later priority change occurs.
The response lead establishes a trusted contact channel and assigns collection, containment and business verification owners with decision times.

Privacy and legal assess exposed message content and notification applicability. Communications prepares a factual update without distributing the phishing content broadly. Authorized activity to test CHG001 is a legitimate retention change on a different mailbox; it does not explain r01.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Compare the exact sender, envelope authentication, Reply To, thread headers and vendor master change audit. Authentication passing does not validate a business instruction. Search other pending payments to SIM-992 and other changes by ap01. Determine whether the supplier mailbox or an internal mailbox was compromised; do not infer either from thread continuity.
phases.source_basis: Scenario-specific response adaptation in the supplied playbook

steps: Finance freezes pay-202 and relevant beneficiary changes under its mandate. If settled, fraud contacts the receiving bank through established channels for recall. Preserve the thread and vendor audit. Restrict the suspicious address without blocking the supplier entire domain when a narrower control works.
phases.source_basis: Scenario-specific response adaptation in the supplied playbook

steps: Restore verified vendor details with dual approval and independent callback. If account compromise is confirmed, use the identity procedure; otherwise fix the payment verification failure.
phases.source_basis: Scenario-specific response adaptation in the supplied playbook

steps: Reconcile queued, released and settled amounts separately with finance sign off. Resume payments only after verified bank details and a second approver confirm the beneficiary.
phases.source_basis: Scenario-specific response adaptation in the supplied playbook

steps: Record confirmed actions, affected scope, business impact, and unresolved questions. Separate verified facts from suspected attribution, claimed theft, and unconfirmed impact.
Document the initial access path or control failure and retain evidence showing each corrective action worked. Assign every remaining evidence gap and residual risk to a named owner.
Have the relevant business, privacy, legal, safety, and service owners record impact and notification decisions where applicable.
Schedule a safe repeat test of the failed control, validate the detection improvement, and obtain business acceptance before closing the incident.
phases.source_basis: Generalized from the playbook closure principles; wording adapted for this scenario

response_plan.bounded_finding: An attempted payment diversion is confirmed and the provided payment was held before release. No financial loss is demonstrated. The source mailbox compromise remains unresolved.

scenarios.category: Ransomware and data extortion
scenarios.title: Encryption detected on a shared file service
scenarios.lead: Incident commander with relevant service owner
scenarios.description: Encryption detected on a shared file service. All telemetry is simulated for training.
scenarios.source_note: Evidence is reproduced from the uploaded playbook.

response_plan.basis: Shared domain response procedure extracted from the supplied playbook.
response_plan.priority_guidance: Declare P1 for active encryption on a shared service, threatened recovery infrastructure or confirmed sensitive exfiltration.
response_plan.response_lead: Incident commander with endpoint and infrastructure teams
response_plan.response_assumption: Treat LT-ENG04 and the FS01 share as actively compromised and preserve the recovery environment. Investigate data theft even if encryption is the first visible symptom.

steps: SOC L1 validates unreadable files with the service owner and correlates EDR writes, SMB access and the .locked extension changes.
SOC L1 records LT-ENG04, eng04, FS01, affected shares and the earliest known change. Preserve ransom notes as evidence without following their instructions.
Endpoint response identifies active writing processes and network sessions. Begin authorized isolation promptly when destructive activity is continuing.
Infrastructure confirms backup administration exposure, immutable copy availability and whether replication can propagate corrupted files or deletes.
SOC L1 checks concurrent identity and outbound transfer alerts. Encryption, extortion claims and confirmed data disclosure are separate findings.
SOC L1 pages the incident commander with observed damage, immediate isolation state, backup concerns and the next required owner.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The incident commander activates P1 response, infrastructure recovery and business continuity under one decision log and trusted communications channel.
The response lead assigns separate endpoint, identity, network, backup and privacy workstreams. Protect clean administrator accounts and recovery stations.
The business owner identifies critical service dependencies, acceptable fallback and restoration order. Record the cost and safety impact of network restrictions.

Legal and communications manage extortion contact and external statements through authorized channels. Technical staff preserve demands and do not make payment commitments. Authorized activity to test CHG004 explains a bulk rename on FS02 but not recovery tampering or the ransom note on LT-ENG04.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: DFIR builds the timeline from initial access through execution, privilege use, discovery, file changes and backup tampering. Preserve representative volatile evidence when feasible.
Endpoint response searches all hosts for the responsible process, parent chain, persistence and remote execution. Separate observed execution from a matching filename.
Identity response traces eng04 and service accounts across privileged sessions, directory changes and management hosts. Look for credentials exposed before encryption.
Infrastructure inventories unique affected files and shares. Keep 1840 writes, 612 remote files and 608 extension changes as separate observations until reconciled.
The backup team independently enumerates restore points, deletion attempts, access history and recovery account changes. A status banner does not establish a clean restore.
Network and privacy teams examine earlier object downloads, archives and outbound transfers. Validate transfer destinations and unique data scope where logs permit.
SOC L2 tests CHG004 against FS02 and its migration scope. It cannot explain recovery tampering or the ransom note on LT-ENG04.
DFIR identifies the last trusted administration and backup boundary. Document missing telemetry and request provider preservation before retention expires.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Endpoint response isolates LT-ENG04 and other confirmed affected hosts while retaining an approved response path. Verify destructive network writes cease.
The file service owner restricts compromised sessions or share writes using the narrowest effective control. Avoid disconnecting clean recovery systems without impact review.
Identity response disables compromised access and terminates relevant privileged and application sessions. Protect emergency access and record enforcement evidence.
The backup owner isolates recovery administration, secures offline credentials and pauses harmful replication where appropriate. Preserve immutable and independent copies.
Network response blocks confirmed command, transfer and lateral paths with an expiry and rollback condition. Check for alternate egress and management channels.

The incident commander verifies containment across endpoints, shares and recovery systems. Expand isolation if fresh encryption, new credentials or backup changes continue. 02 Eradication recovery and closure
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Endpoint and infrastructure teams rebuild compromised systems from verified images when control of privileged execution cannot be established reliably.
Identity response rotates affected secrets in dependency order from clean administration stations. Replace persistence in accounts, tasks, services and remote management.
Application owners repair the validated initial access flaw and remove unauthorized access paths before restored data returns to production.
The backup team validates restore media, software and administration integrity. Preserve originals and document any unavoidable evidence loss from emergency recovery.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Infrastructure restores a representative backup into an isolated recovery segment and checks malware, configuration, permissions and application integrity before expansion.
Data owners reconcile restored records, files and transactions against authoritative sources. Measure actual data loss and recovery time against business objectives.
Business owners authorize staged service return with monitored writes, working telemetry, clean administrator access and a defined rollback trigger.
SOC continues hunting for the entry path and persistence across the restored population. New encryption or unexplained privilege use stops the rollout.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: DFIR distinguishes confirmed encryption, confirmed theft and extortion claims. Record backup integrity findings and remaining data scope uncertainty separately.
The response lead records the initial access cause, spread path and corrective controls with verification evidence and accountable owners.
Privacy, legal and business owners complete notification and customer impact decisions. Track financial, operational and unrecovered data effects.
The incident commander closes only after accepted restoration and assigned residual risks, then schedules a restore exercise and detection review.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

response_plan.basis: Shared domain response procedure extracted from the supplied playbook.
response_plan.priority_guidance: Declare P1 for confirmed cross customer sensitive disclosure or critical financial changes. Escalate public metadata access that exposes production credentials.
response_plan.response_lead: Application security with SOC L2 and privacy
response_plan.response_assumption: Treat the statements07 route as disclosing other customers data through a valid token. Scope authorization, metadata access and write operations independently.

steps: SOC L1 preserves the alert, request IDs, response codes, requesting identity and object identifiers. Avoid copying full customer statements into ordinary tickets.
Application security validates cust070 against the authoritative owner of stmt071 and stmt072. URL patterns and success codes alone cannot establish ownership.
SOC L1 checks whether object content was actually returned. Preserve storage or response audit that links req707 to the delivered object.
The service owner identifies the vulnerable build, affected route and any shared authorization or cache component. Record when that version entered service.
SOC L1 distinguishes an authentication problem from missing object authorization, unsafe fields or internal fetch access. Select immediate controls by the proven behavior.
SOC L1 escalates the sensitive disclosure with token t707, known objects, current control state and the highest value missing audit.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The incident commander appoints application security and the service owner to lead, with SOC L2, identity, privacy and cloud response support.
The application owner defines which route can be disabled or restricted safely and the approved fallback for genuine customers.
Privacy begins a unique object and affected person assessment while SOC preserves available audit. Do not wait for a complete subject count to contain disclosure.

The response lead records change authority, rollback trigger, notification owner and the next evidence collection deadline in one incident record. Authorized activity to test The support read includes a caseworker role and SUP007 authorization; validate that ticket before excluding it.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Application security maps the request subject, tenant, token scope, object owner, operation and response outcome for every suspicious request.
SOC L2 joins API gateway, application, authorization, cache and storage records by request ID. Preserve original logs alongside normalized query results.
Application engineering reviews authorization placement in the affected build and sibling routes. Check object reads, exports, updates and privileged fields.
Identity response examines issuance and later use of t707 and related tokens. Determine whether abuse required credential theft or ordinary customer access sufficed.
Cloud response investigates any internal fetch and metadata credential use in parallel. Trace derived credentials to downstream storage and role activity.
The data owner deduplicates returned objects and recipients. A 420 request aggregate is neither 420 customers nor proof of 420 successful disclosures.
SOC L2 validates the SUP007 support access against role, ticket, object and time. An approved support action does not authorize cust070.
Application security reproduces the boundary only in an isolated tenant with synthetic identities. Record missing logs and version exposure limits.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The service owner disables the vulnerable route or deploys an independently verified authorization guard. Check normal service and cross owner denial immediately.
Identity response revokes t707 and associated compromised credentials as justified. Confirm denial at the API rather than accepting an identity console acknowledgement.
Application engineering invalidates shared caches and blocks alternate paths that can return the same protected objects without authorization.
Cloud response restricts internal fetch egress and exposed workload credentials if metadata access is involved. Test old resource access after revocation.
Finance holds unauthorized pending operations where write or mass assignment abuse affects payments. Preserve before and after business records before correction.
SOC L2 watches all affected routes for continued mismatched ownership and successful export. Rate limits may reduce volume but do not repair authorization. 03 Eradication recovery and closure
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Application engineering implements server enforced subject, tenant, object and action authorization on every relevant path, including cache retrieval and bulk operations.
The service owner removes unsafe writable fields and separates privileged administrative operations from ordinary customer updates with explicit approval checks.
Cloud engineering replaces exposed workload identities, constrains resource permissions and repairs metadata or destination validation failures when present.
Application security reviews sibling implementations and release tests, then preserves the vulnerable and corrected build digests for the incident record.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Application security tests allowed same owner access and denied cross owner access with two synthetic tenants, including fallback, cache and export paths.
The service owner deploys gradually, validates error rates and confirms legitimate customer workflows without weakening the new authorization boundary.
Data and finance owners reconcile exposed objects, changed fields and financial outcomes. Document populations that cannot be reconstructed from available audit.
SOC verifies working request and authorization telemetry and assigns a monitoring owner before unrestricted service returns.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: SOC L2 records the minimum confirmed returned objects and separates likely exposure from unknown historical scope with evidence IDs.
Application security documents the failed boundary, vulnerable versions and regression coverage, including all sibling routes reviewed.
Privacy and business owners record customer communication and notification decisions with the applicable basis and unresolved evidence requests.
The incident owner obtains service acceptance and tracks remaining remediation, log coverage and access reviews to completion.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: SOC L1 validates failure from independent external probes and service desk reports. Record affected regions, customer functions and first observed degradation.
The network team checks circuit utilization, loss and routing. Moderate bandwidth does not exclude an application layer request flood.
The application SRE checks authentication workers, database waits, queues and latency. Preserve baseline and current metrics with measurement units.
SOC L1 compares the 18000 requests per second with normal demand and the approved campaign route. Record confidence in the abnormal traffic cluster.
Fraud operations reviews successful suspicious logins and risky payments while availability response proceeds. An outage must not suspend financial monitoring.
SOC L1 pages network response, the application SRE and the incident commander with the actual bottleneck, failed customer checks and available provider contacts.

steps: The incident commander opens P1 response and names a network lead, application SRE, provider liaison, fraud owner and communications owner.

The provider liaison uses verified emergency contacts and supplies affected prefixes, request patterns, start time and current routing evidence.

steps: Network response compares upstream counters, clean side traffic and firewall drops to locate whether the real constraint is before or after the edge.
The application SRE correlates route, request fingerprint, authentication outcome and backend work. Distinguish valid TLS from authorized useful demand.
SOC L2 reviews source diversity, automation fingerprints and behavior without treating every source IP as an attributable attacker.
The SRE tests whether retries, expensive preauthentication operations or cache misses amplify load. Preserve configurations and representative bounded samples.
The provider liaison checks direct origin exposure and paths bypassing the protection service. Verify affected addresses and anycast or regional behavior.
Fraud investigates the 12 successful clustered logins and the separate beneficiary alert. Link them to the flood only when evidence supports it.
SOC L2 tests CHG010 against its offers path and expected volume. A legitimate campaign does not explain exhaustion of the login service.
Cloud response reconciles provider billing, token metering and client retries for AI exhaustion variants. Separate attempted, served and billed demand.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The SRE enables scoped application challenges, rate limits and bounded queues based on behavior and route while checking genuine customer success.
The provider diverts affected traffic through approved scrubbing when upstream capacity is constrained. Verify clean side counters and route propagation.
Network response restricts origin access to approved protection paths where feasible. Preserve a clean administration and emergency customer access route.
The SRE limits concurrency, expensive work and runaway retries. Use controlled fallback and budget caps for inference services, recording functionality lost.
The incident commander authorizes narrowly scoped provider filters or blackholing only with documented service impact, expiry and rollback conditions.

SOC and fraud compare postchange availability, latency, false challenges and suspicious transactions. Escalate if mitigation moves the bottleneck or enables another loss. 04 Eradication recovery and closure
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Engineering removes unnecessary expensive unauthenticated processing and implements enforceable request size, concurrency, retry and resource budgets.
Network engineering closes direct origin bypass and documents provider protections, emergency routes and tested failover capacity.
Cloud and application owners replace exposed service keys and constrain client authority where misuse or leaked credentials enabled exhaustion.
Detection engineering updates service health and abuse correlations using reviewed demand baselines and known legitimate campaigns.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The SRE demonstrates external login and critical transaction success from affected regions with latency and errors inside approved service targets.
Network response removes emergency restrictions gradually with the provider, checking route convergence, loss and continued protection at each stage.
Finance and cloud owners reconcile unexpected charges and emergency resources. Retain spending controls and provider billing evidence until exposure is understood.
The service owner accepts normal operation after agreed stable intervals, working fraud monitoring and an explicit trigger to reapply mitigation.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: SOC records the constrained resource, observed attack behavior and customer impact. Keep flood linkage to fraud or account compromise evidence bounded.
The provider liaison retains routing changes, scrubbing results and mitigation decisions so effectiveness can be reviewed independently.
The business owner records downtime, customer effects and continuity performance; legal evaluates applicable notifications and contractual reporting.
The incident commander assigns capacity, origin protection and runbook improvements, then schedules a bounded load and failover exercise.

steps: SOC L1 preserves database export, archive creation, proxy upload and DLP observations with restricted case access and source retention details.

Identity response reviews sessions, source devices, unusual authentication, delegated access and other actors that could have used analyst13 credentials.
The insider risk lead compares the export with approved job duties, tickets and policy. Test CHG013 against its different actor and managed destination.
SOC L2 reviews earlier exports, removable media and uploads within an authorized time interval. Expand access only when the evidence justifies it.
Database and PAM owners check privilege changes, audit suppression and financial updates if administrator misuse is suspected. Use replica and independent logs for gaps.
Privacy and legal determine what the organization can establish about external retention, onward access and recovery. Record unknowns rather than asserting deletion.

steps: The authorized manager and identity owner suspend risky export or privileged capabilities while preserving the account and audit state as evidence.

steps: Physical security checks immediate safety and secures the affected area. SOC records the report without confronting the unknown person.
SOC L1 preserves access control, camera, switch and DHCP records. Record local camera time, UTC time and any clock difference.
Network response identifies Gi1/0/16, the observed MAC and lease for 10.16.0.90. Verify the exact port before any disconnection.
Asset management checks approved contractors and device inventory. CHG016 concerns a different printer MAC and does not identify DEV16 as authorized.
SOC L1 checks the 74 destination scan and any successful authentication. Link network observations to a session rather than assuming MAC addresses are immutable.
SOC L1 escalates with room, port, device, safety state and requested quarantine. Include evidence retention deadlines for footage and access logs.

steps: The incident commander appoints physical security and network response leads, with facilities, endpoint response, privacy and DFIR as required.
Facilities determines emergency egress and critical equipment constraints before door or power changes. The qualified owner controls any safety process.
The response lead documents authority to acquire a device or review footage and keeps physical evidence handling linked to the cyber incident.

The business owner approves an alternative for affected room services. Legal and communications direct external reports and customer statements when applicable. Authorized activity to test CHG016 is a printer with a different MAC and does not explain DEV16.

steps: Network response correlates door observations, port activation, DHCP lease and scan timing. Keep a reported entry separate from the observed network activity.
Physical security reviews the authorized camera interval, badge sequence, escort records and maintenance tickets. Document gaps and uncertainty in identity.
SOC L2 identifies every destination and protocol contacted by DEV16 and checks for successful login, file access or configuration changes.
DFIR acquires the device through an approved method and preserves identifiers, storage and volatile data when justified. Do not attach it to a normal analyst network.
Endpoint response reviews unattended workstations and relevant USB events if removable media or local interaction is possible.
For lost devices, identity and MDM owners compare possession time, encryption evidence age, token use and actual lock or wipe acknowledgement.
Asset owners verify approved devices independently; a room label, matching vendor name or adjacent legitimate change is insufficient authorization.
SOC L2 scopes exposed credentials, local cached data and reachable services. Record unavailable footage, offline endpoints and uncertain physical custody explicitly.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Network response quarantines the verified port or NAC session with the service owner aware of affected equipment. Confirm internal access from the device stops.
Physical security secures the room and preserves the device with a custody record. Facilities maintains safe emergency exit and essential systems.
Identity response revokes affected device trust, account sessions or certificates when exposure is plausible. Verify resource access denial independently of physical possession.
Endpoint response isolates workstations with supported removable media execution and preserves the USB safely. Do not execute a file to confirm its purpose.
The MDM owner requests lock or wipe only under approved authority after preserving available evidence. Record offline or queued actions as pending.
SOC L2 searches for continued access from other ports, credentials or cloud sessions. Escalate if physical containment leaves an active digital path. 06 Eradication recovery and closure

steps: Facilities repairs the verified room access, escort or unattended equipment weakness and reviews the relevant authorized access list.
Endpoint response rebuilds compromised workstations and removes unauthorized devices or persistence after evidence collection and owner approval.
Identity and network owners replace exposed credentials, device certificates and profiles, then remove unauthorized connectivity and excessive local access.
Asset management updates inventory and ownership; detection engineering tests port, rogue device and removable media visibility using benign approved equipment.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Network and facilities owners validate expected equipment availability, safe door behavior and approved room access after restrictions are adjusted.
Identity response tests rejection of old credentials and device trust. Recovered laptops require acquisition and integrity review before a managed rebuild.
Privacy and data owners reconcile cached and cloud data exposure, using current encryption evidence and actual activity rather than assuming a lost device stayed protected.
The service owner accepts restoration with working NAC, endpoint telemetry and physical monitoring, plus a trigger for renewed unknown device activity.

steps: SOC records the observed device and network effects without claiming the tailgater installed it unless independent evidence supports that link.
Physical security and DFIR retain custody, footage references and collection authority. Document any period of uncontrolled possession.

steps: SOC L2 joins fingerprint f19 to successful sessions, device changes, beneficiary additions and payment outcomes using stable request and session IDs.
Customer identity engineering examines credential exposure, authentication decisions, factor changes, recovery events and prior session issuance.
Fraud reviews each of the 14 successful accounts for unauthorized actions and the customer verification result. Record confirmed, probable and unknown compromise separately.
Payments traces recipients, settlement, recall and any split or repeated transfers. Confirm final loss independently of a queued transaction status.
Identity engineering checks SIM change, recovery and app session reuse paths where relevant. Telecom restoration and client logout do not necessarily end server access.
SOC L2 compares approved known device activity for cust191 and assesses shared networks or fingerprints before making account exclusions.
Application engineering reviews token storage, session invalidation and device registration boundaries using synthetic accounts in an isolated test environment.
Privacy deduplicates downloaded objects and affected customers. Record audit coverage limits and request provider or telecom preservation through authorized contacts.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Customer identity engineering invalidates confirmed risky sessions at the service and blocks affected tokens. Verify old read and payment requests are denied.
Fraud holds suspicious transfers and new beneficiary use, or initiates recall for settled funds through established contacts. Record acknowledgement and outcome.
The access team applies scoped behavior and credential stuffing controls while preserving legitimate customer recovery. Avoid indiscriminate lockout solely by shared IP.
Customer care stops unsafe recovery through a disputed phone number and uses the approved independent identity verification path.
Application owners suspend unsafe device enrollment or recovery functions when a confirmed flaw permits continued takeover, with a documented customer fallback.
SOC and fraud monitor postcontrol successful access, new payees and transaction attempts. A continuing old session triggers renewed containment. 07 Eradication recovery and closure

steps: Customer identity engineering removes unauthorized factors, devices, beneficiaries and recovery changes after the real customer is verified.
The identity owner replaces exposed credentials and strengthens recovery and high risk transaction checks against the validated entry path.
Application engineering implements server enforced session invalidation and protects tokens, device binding and sensitive actions with explicit authorization.
Fraud and detection engineering add validated behavioral correlations and breached credential checks, reviewing impact on genuine customer access.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Customer care confirms that the verified customer controls the approved authentication and recovery methods and can access the account safely.
Identity engineering proves old sessions and removed devices fail at the server while normal authenticated workflows succeed.

Fraud authorizes staged removal of temporary restrictions with monitored transactions and an assigned review of the remaining successful accounts.

response_plan.priority_guidance: Start at P2 for limited mailbox access. Declare P1 for broad application permissions, privileged persistence, production secrets or material sensitive disclosure.
response_plan.response_lead: Identity application owner with email responder
response_plan.response_assumption: Treat notes23 and grant g2323 as unauthorized delegated mailbox access that survives a password reset. Investigate user, application and workload identities separately.

steps: SOC L1 captures the exact application ID, user object, grant ID, permission scopes and resource. Display names alone cannot reliably identify an application.
Identity response determines whether the access is delegated user consent or application permission and whether the consent was administrative or individual.
SOC L1 preserves sign in, consent and resource audit, including activity after the password reset. Record observed access rather than assuming reset completed containment.
The resource owner checks the actual mailbox reads and any sends, downloads or modifications. Distinguish requested permission from exercised permission.
Identity response checks current privileged roles, unauthorized factors, added secrets and other users granting the same application access.
SOC L1 escalates with notes23, g2323, confirmed resource activity, current privileges and the required application or identity restriction.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The incident commander appoints identity response and the application owner, with email, cloud, DFIR and privacy support according to actual access.
The identity owner identifies clean emergency administration and assigns authorized executors for account, device, grant and workload credential changes.
The business owner maps dependencies on the affected identity and approves controlled replacement or fallback so containment does not strand critical recovery.

The response lead opens a persistence and permission workstream beyond password reset and records the next resource level verification time. Authorized activity to test The approved orion-notes app has a different identifier and only profile scope.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: SOC L2 joins consent, delegated sign ins and resource audit for notes23 and session s2323. Keep token references and original source records.
Identity response enumerates grants, application roles, service principal credentials, owners and federated trust settings for the exact application object.
The email owner scopes read, send, forwarding and delegated activity across the available interval. Deduplicate message IDs before claiming unique message counts.
SOC L2 searches all users and tenants within authorized scope for related consent or resource activity. Record the population actually covered by audit.
Identity response checks unauthorized MFA registration, role activation and secret addition. A compromised user may have created a separate persistent workload credential.
Cloud response traces exposed repository or application secrets to resource reads, role assignments and new infrastructure, including downstream secrets accessed.
SOC L2 compares the approved orion notes consent by identifier and permission. Similar branding does not explain the rogue application scope.
DFIR investigates the credential or consent entry path where evidence is incomplete. Record postreset access as survival of the old control path, not a new infection.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The application owner disables or restricts notes23 and revokes g2323 under authorized administration. Verify old resource requests fail after the change.
Identity response blocks affected user sessions and removes unauthorized factors after preservation. Coordinate application session termination separately where required.
The workload owner disables exposed application secrets, federated credentials or keys and restricts downstream resource permissions. Test each affected identity independently.
Cloud and email owners constrain unauthorized roles, grants, forwarding and new resources while preserving before and after configuration evidence.
The response lead stages replacement identities for critical services and keeps clean emergency access available. Record business impact and rollback conditions.

SOC L2 searches for postrevocation use, derived sessions and newly created credentials. Continued resource access requires renewed containment at the resource boundary. 08 Eradication recovery and closure

steps: Identity response removes rogue principals, consent and persistence after evidence preservation, and rotates every confirmed exposed dependent secret in a controlled sequence.
The identity owner reenrolls legitimate authentication methods from a trusted device and eliminates the verified consent or privilege escalation weakness.
Application owners replace broad long lived credentials with scoped managed or federated identities where supported and maintain accountable ownership.
Detection engineering correlates consent, factor, role and resource actions, testing approved benign enrollment and administrative changes before deployment.

steps: Resource owners demonstrate denial of the old user, application and workload access paths that were affected, retaining exact test identities and timestamps.
The business owner verifies legitimate applications and critical scheduled jobs work with replacement credentials and expected least privilege permissions.
Privacy and resource owners reconcile all accessible or accessed content, including uncertainty from missing message IDs or resource logging gaps.
Identity response confirms audit coverage, clean administration and monitored restart before temporary restrictions are removed.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: SOC records confirmed identity types, persistence mechanisms and resource effects without treating a password reset as proof that all access ended.
The application and identity owners retain the credential inventory, removal evidence, deny tests and dependency checks supporting recovery.
Privacy and legal record disclosure and reporting decisions; the incident owner assigns unresolved historical access and provider evidence to named owners.
The response lead schedules a safe consent and credential revocation exercise and tracks orphaned applications and excessive permissions to resolution.

response_plan.priority_guidance: Declare P1 for broad trusted remote execution or production privilege. A provider notice without local impact may start at P2 while exposure is established.
response_plan.response_lead: Incident commander with vendor manager and endpoint response
response_plan.response_assumption: Treat MSP job j2525 as unauthorized remote execution through a trusted supplier channel. Investigate the vendor control plane and every local target rather than relying on vendor assurances.

steps: SOC L1 validates the vendor through an independent registered contact and requests the exact remote job, operator, target list and maintenance authority.
Endpoint response preserves RMM job j2525, script metadata, process ancestry and account creation evidence without rerunning the job.
SOC L1 separates eight reported completed targets from four pending hosts. A pending job remains exposure until cancellation is verified.
The vendor manager checks the approved service scope, maintenance ticket and relevant contract contact. A trusted tool does not authorize every instruction.
SOC L1 checks local egress, privileged sessions, SaaS connector exports and partner VPN access for effects beyond the provider notice.
SOC L1 escalates with the trusted channel, local impact, active credentials, pending actions and current vendor response state.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The incident commander assigns vendor management, endpoint response, identity, network and business continuity leads under one local incident record.
The supplier liaison opens a provider incident and requests evidence preservation, affected tenant scope, timeline and containment results in writing.
The business owner approves service fallback and temporary supplier access restrictions. Record critical dependencies that cannot simply be disconnected.

Privacy and legal assess contractual and statutory notifications using verified local and supplier impact, retaining uncertainty when provider investigation is incomplete. Authorized activity to test j2500 is tied to CHG025 and verified content; trusted tool use alone cannot distinguish the malicious job.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: SOC L2 correlates RMM job IDs, operator sessions and endpoint process trees across all 12 targets, including output and partial execution results.
Endpoint DFIR investigates new accounts, services, tasks, file changes and credential access on completed hosts, preserving representative volatile evidence where justified.
Identity response reviews vendor accounts, API keys, federated trust and privileged sessions before and after the reported compromise.
Network response examines supplier VPN segments, unintended cross zone rules and destinations outside the approved integration scope.
SaaS owners compare connector schedule, key use, destination and object volume with local audit. A provider notice does not prove causation of every export.
The vendor liaison requests control plane evidence and checks it against local observations. Record conflicting times, missing fields and unverified provider assertions.
SOC L2 tests approved job j2500 and CHG025 by target, signer, content and time. Verified maintenance cannot authorize j2525 by association.
Privacy and data owners deduplicate exposed objects and customers, while DFIR scopes any downstream identities or other services sharing the vendor trust path.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The RMM owner pauses j2525 and disables affected vendor sessions or integration keys after preserving the control plane audit. Confirm pending targets cannot execute.
Endpoint response isolates confirmed affected hosts in approved stages, with clean recovery access and a business fallback for essential services.
Identity response revokes vendor credentials and unauthorized local accounts, checking derived sessions and alternate support identities independently.
Network response replaces excessive partner access with a verified allowlist and blocks confirmed transfer paths without severing unrelated recovery channels.
SaaS owners disable exposed connector keys and pause unsafe exports, preserving queued work and providing a controlled manual or read only fallback.
The response lead verifies local denial and requests supplier containment evidence. Escalate continued activity even when the supplier reports the issue resolved. 09 Eradication recovery and closure
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Endpoint teams remove persistence or rebuild affected hosts from trusted images when execution scope cannot be established reliably.
Vendor and identity owners replace compromised integration credentials and validate the supplier administration path before trust is reintroduced.
Network and SaaS owners repair broad segmentation rules, excessive connector scope, missing expiry and weak approval for privileged supplier actions.
Supplier management records required remediation, independent evidence and unresolved exceptions, with owners and dates instead of accepting a generic assurance letter.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Endpoint response validates each target individually, including partial and pending jobs, and confirms no unauthorized account or remote task persists.
The business owner tests a bounded legitimate supplier task through a verified account with least privilege, session recording and explicit expiry.
SaaS and data owners reconcile exported objects, destination and provider scope; record unresolved retention or cross tenant exposure explicitly.
The incident commander restores supplier access gradually only after local tests and provider evidence meet the agreed acceptance criteria.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: SOC records the supplier trust path, known executed targets and data effects, separating provider compromise from unproven causal links.
Vendor management retains preservation requests, evidence, remediation commitments and contractual reporting decisions with the incident record.
Business and privacy owners sign off service restoration, affected data scope and any continuing supplier risk or monitoring requirement.
The response lead tests supplier credential revocation and pending job cancellation in a later exercise and tracks access recertification improvements.

response_plan.response_assumption: Treat GW28 as compromised because unauthorized execution, export, scanning and account creation are observed. Verify the actual vulnerability and downstream access without assuming a CVE from an advisory alone.

steps: SOC L1 confirms GW28 identity, exposed interface, installed build and business role from authoritative inventory and independent network records.
Network response preserves appliance audit, running configuration, accounts and relevant logs through vendor supported methods before destructive repair when feasible.
SOC L1 correlates the unexpected process, configuration export, internal scan and new support28 account. An advisory alone is not exploitation evidence.
The service owner checks redundancy and clean administration access before isolation. Avoid losing the only route used to coordinate response.
Identity response identifies secrets, certificates and sessions potentially accessible to the device. Flag credentials trusted by internal services.
SOC L1 pages the incident commander and network DFIR lead with current internal reach, service impact and the required containment path.

steps: The incident commander activates perimeter, identity, application, DFIR and infrastructure workstreams under a trusted out of band response channel.
The network owner selects a clean failover or approved service pause and records the expected customer and branch impact.
The vendor liaison requests validated collection and rebuild guidance for the exact product and build, preserving the original device state where possible.

The business owner and privacy team assess downstream service, configuration and sensitive data exposure while containment proceeds. Authorized activity to test CHG028 is a recorded diagnostic on another gateway and does not authorize support28.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: DFIR correlates request req2828, unexpected process execution, export, scanning and account creation with source and receive times preserved.
Network response compares current configuration, administrative users, keys, certificates, routes and logging settings with a known trusted baseline.
Identity response reviews internal authentication from GW28, exposed VPN secrets and new sessions that could survive replacement of the appliance.
SOC L2 scopes all 120 scanned destinations and checks successful access, file reads or new administration rather than equating scanning with compromise.
Application DFIR inspects related public servers for unexpected files and child processes, preserving artefacts without invoking suspected web content.
Network response investigates DNS and outbound traffic and seeks independent flow evidence if local device audit may have been altered.
SOC L2 validates CHG028 on GW29 and any vendor diagnostic scope. It does not authorize support28 or unexplained changes on GW28.
DFIR verifies advisory applicability to the installed build and observed entry path. Document unknown exploit details and missing appliance telemetry explicitly.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Network response restricts GW28 management and internal reach or fails over to a verified clean device under approved emergency authority.
Identity response disables unauthorized support accounts and revokes affected secrets and sessions, prioritizing credentials that grant internal administration.
Network response blocks confirmed command and transfer destinations and restricts lateral paths while retaining clean response access and required service monitoring.
Endpoint response isolates internal hosts with evidence of follow on execution or privileged access, linked to the same incident and scope map.
Application owners remove compromised server instances from load balancing and constrain unsafe upload or execution paths when web compromise is involved.
SOC L2 verifies no continued scanning, unauthorized login or data transfer across independent sources. Reapply containment when an alternate path survives. 10 Eradication recovery and closure
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Infrastructure rebuilds or replaces compromised gateways and servers from trusted images and applies the verified fix for the actual entry path.
Identity and PKI owners rotate exposed secrets and certificates in dependency order, terminating resource sessions that could outlive the device.
Network engineering removes public administration, unnecessary services, unauthorized rules and account persistence, with a reviewed configuration baseline.
The service owner validates deployment and management integrity, because patching a controlled device alone does not remove prior persistence or stolen credentials.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Network response tests approved routing, VPN and customer service through the clean replacement while prohibited management and internal paths remain denied.
Identity response proves old device credentials and certificates cannot access affected resources. Save the test result and new trust inventory.
DFIR and SOC hunt downstream destinations over the available interval and record hosts that lacked sufficient telemetry for a firm compromise decision.
The business owner accepts staged restoration with log forwarding, monitoring, clean emergency administration and a tested rollback option.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: DFIR records confirmed execution and configuration effects, the validated or unknown entry path and the searched downstream population.
The network owner retains collection records, original configuration, rebuild provenance and fix applicability with the incident evidence.
Privacy and business owners complete disclosure and service impact decisions, assigning unresolved secret exposure or provider evidence to named owners.
The incident commander closes after verified restoration and schedules an external exposure and emergency failover review.

steps: Preserve independent firewall flow and destination authentication data before changing the device. Treat unauthorized management and core access as P1. Identify a clean out of band management path.

steps: The incident commander activates perimeter, identity, application, DFIR and infrastructure workstreams under a trusted out of band response channel.
The network owner selects a clean failover or approved service pause and records the expected customer and branch impact.
The vendor liaison requests validated collection and rebuild guidance for the exact product and build, preserving the original device state where possible.

The business owner and privacy team assess downstream service, configuration and sensitive data exposure while containment proceeds. Authorized activity to test CHG028 is a recorded diagnostic on another gateway and does not authorize support28.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Join a3030 to rule creation and logging changes, then follow ALLOW-TEMP30 to CORE30. Compare running configuration to a known good version and inspect all admin accounts, API tokens and management routes.
phases.source_basis: Scenario-specific response adaptation in the supplied playbook

steps: Terminate the administrator session, restrict management to approved networks and disable admin30. Remove ALLOW-TEMP30 after preserving it and isolate CORE30 as required; restore log forwarding with verification.
phases.source_basis: Scenario-specific response adaptation in the supplied playbook

steps: Rotate exposed management and service credentials and remove unauthorized policy changes. Apply MFA and eliminate public management access through controlled architecture changes.
phases.source_basis: Scenario-specific response adaptation in the supplied playbook

steps: Validate approved connectivity and expected deny tests from an external test location. Verify audit delivery, configuration diff and CORE30 integrity before closure.
phases.source_basis: Scenario-specific response adaptation in the supplied playbook

steps: Record confirmed actions, affected scope, business impact, and unresolved questions. Separate verified facts from suspected attribution, claimed theft, and unconfirmed impact.
Document the initial access path or control failure and retain evidence showing each corrective action worked. Assign every remaining evidence gap and residual risk to a named owner.
Have the relevant business, privacy, legal, safety, and service owners record impact and notification decisions where applicable.
Schedule a safe repeat test of the failed control, validate the detection improvement, and obtain business acceptance before closing the incident.

tools.name: Proofpoint
tools.role: Email security and initial-delivery evidence
tools.investigate: initial exploit delivery or administrator credential phishing when evidenced. Preserve message ID, headers, verdicts, recipients, URLs and attachment hashes where available.
tools.actions: Quarantine/purge only confirmed malicious messages through approved mail-security workflows. Search for campaign-wide recipients and post-delivery exposure.
tools.when_not_applicable: If there is no supported email vector or relevant telemetry, document why Proofpoint is not implicated instead of inventing a finding.

tools.name: CrowdStrike Falcon
tools.role: Endpoint detection, execution and host scope
tools.investigate: web/server process trees, web shells, file changes, shell commands, persistence and credential access. Pivot by host/device ID, user, process tree, file hash and UTC event time.
tools.actions: Use approved host containment/remediation only when evidence and incident authority justify it. Record detection/host IDs and action results.
tools.when_not_applicable: If no endpoint is implicated or telemetry is unavailable, document the gap and continue with other relevant sources.

tools.name: ExtraHop
tools.role: Network detection, movement and egress correlation
tools.investigate: inbound patterns, server-to-internal connections, C2, unusual egress and data transfer. Pivot by source/destination, DNS, protocol, device and UTC time window.
tools.actions: Preserve alert/record identifiers and distinguish observed traffic from inferred intent. Escalate missing visibility as an evidence gap.
tools.when_not_applicable: No observed traffic is not proof of no activity. Record sensor coverage and seek approved alternate telemetry.

tools.name: ServiceNow
tools.role: Incident record, coordination and audit trail
tools.investigate: Create/link the incident and correlate findings from Proofpoint, Falcon and ExtraHop using stable IDs and timestamps. Maintain one authoritative timeline.
tools.actions: Track severity rationale, affected assets/CIs, evidence links, task owners, approvals, communications, containment results, recovery tests and closure sign-off.
tools.when_not_applicable: If ServiceNow is unavailable in the exercise, use a clearly labeled mock ticket rather than implying a real ticket exists.

tool_workflow.correlation_keys: Scenario ID, UTC timestamps, user/principal, host/device ID, source/destination IP, DNS/domain, message ID, URL/file hash, process/detection ID, API/request/session ID where relevant, affected asset/CI and ServiceNow incident number. Use only identifiers relevant to this scenario.
tool_workflow.scenario_specific_check: Use the scenario evidence IDs and UTC timeline to confirm the actual attack path. Record which tools have findings, which are inconclusive, and which are not applicable.
tool_workflow.containment_plan: Restrict the exposed service, apply tested compensating controls, preserve evidence and rebuild from trusted baseline where needed.
service_now_fields: Short description with scenario ID and confirmed incident type
Severity and rationale tied to business impact

UTC timeline and stable evidence identifiers

Facts, hypotheses and evidence gaps clearly separated

safety_guardrails: Start with read-only investigation where feasible and preserve original evidence and timestamps.
Obtain incident-command, system-owner and change approvals before disruptive actions.
Do not claim a product action succeeded unless its result is recorded and independently verified.
Do not paste passwords, tokens, private keys or unnecessary customer/employee data into ServiceNow.

response_plan.basis: Shared domain response procedure extracted from the supplied playbook.
response_plan.priority_guidance: Declare P1 for credible unsafe physical conditions, loss of essential control or safety visibility, or a critical service threatened by environmental failure.
response_plan.response_lead: OT operations and safety lead with incident commander
response_plan.response_assumption: Treat the CTRL31 configuration change and independently observed cooling degradation as a safety relevant incident. Qualified operators control the physical process throughout response.

steps: OT operations confirms actual physical conditions using independent sensors and direct operator observation. A normal dashboard does not overrule a verified unsafe condition.
The safety lead determines immediate stabilization and evacuation requirements under the site procedure, keeping people protection ahead of cyber collection.
SOC L1 records CTRL31, ENG31, room, setpoint changes and observed temperature, retaining units and source time zones.
OT engineering preserves passive traffic, controller audit, engineering workstation sessions and the trusted configuration baseline through supported methods.
Facilities checks redundancy, emergency access, interlocks and manual control readiness before any device or network disconnection.
SOC L1 declares the safety concern to the incident commander and OT owner with the physical state, unknowns and currently authorized control path.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The incident commander appoints the qualified OT operations authority and safety lead. SOC and DFIR provide evidence and technical options.
The process owner selects an approved safe mode or manual fallback and records the operating limits that containment must preserve.
The response lead separates process stabilization, engineering investigation, cyber access control and IT service continuity tasks with named decision owners.

Facilities and business continuity prepare environmental or customer service fallback; legal and communications assess reporting based on verified physical and service impact. Authorized activity to test CHG031 covers CTRL32 and does not authorize CTRL31 setpoint changes.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: OT engineering correlates setpoint changes, workstation sessions, controller writes and independent sensor trends, keeping commands separate from actual process effects.
DFIR investigates ENG31 and the remote engineering identity using approved passive collection and the operator agreed acquisition plan.
The process owner compares controller logic, settings, firmware and schedules with the verified engineering baseline and approved change history.
SOC L2 traces the engineering path and affected credentials across gateways and similar controllers without running untested active scans on production equipment.
OT engineering checks mapping and historian integrity when values differ from independent gauges. Consider sensor failure and calibration as alternatives.
Physical security reviews related room or controller access only within authorized scope, including unexplained remote unlocks and cloud integration tokens.
SOC L2 validates CHG031 against CTRL32 and its supervised test. It cannot authorize the altered setpoint on CTRL31.
The safety lead records causal uncertainty, physical observations and evidence gaps. Request vendor support for collection that could alter controller state.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The qualified operator places the process in its approved safe mode and uses local control if required. Document the actual physical result.
Network response restricts the compromised engineering path only after OT confirms essential control, alarms and safety visibility will remain available.
The identity owner disables affected remote engineering sessions or cloud connector tokens in a coordinated change witnessed by operations.
OT engineering stops unauthorized changes and preserves controller state before restoration when safe. Avoid power cycling solely to remove a cyber indicator.
Facilities and physical security protect controlled areas while preserving emergency egress. Local guards or manual processes support necessary continuity.
The operator and SOC verify both physical stabilization and stopped unauthorized commands. A network deny result alone does not prove the process is safe. 11 Eradication recovery and closure
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: OT engineering restores validated controller logic and configuration through the approved engineering change process, retaining the original affected state as evidence.
Endpoint response rebuilds compromised engineering workstations and identity owners replace exposed engineering credentials without disrupting safety dependent services.
The process owner validates firmware and integration provenance and repairs the proven remote access or excessive permission weakness.
OT monitoring owners restore trustworthy sensor mapping, passive monitoring and alarm delivery, using supported tests and vendor guidance where needed.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The safety lead verifies independent measurements remain within the approved operating band and witnesses alarm, interlock and loss of signal behavior.
OT engineering compares the restored configuration with the trusted baseline and tests authorized commands under a maintenance permit.
The process owner gradually restores remote functions only after old sessions fail and the approved manual fallback remains available.
Business owners reconcile affected production, building conditions and dependent IT service effects before accepting automated operation.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The incident record separates unauthorized commands, verified process changes and inferred attacker intent, including any sensor or historian integrity gap.
OT and safety authorities retain stabilization evidence, engineering approvals, functional test results and any residual operating constraints.
Legal, facilities and business owners record applicable notifications and physical or customer impact without substituting cyber severity for safety assessment.
The incident commander schedules a joint safe shutdown and monitoring exercise and tracks engineering access and segmentation improvements.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

response_plan.response_lead: Software supply chain responder with endpoint and development teams
response_plan.response_assumption: Treat build b4040 and its deployed artefact as untrusted after unexpected dependency execution and secret access. Investigate source, build, signing, distribution and consumers as separate trust stages.

steps: SOC L1 preserves the dependency version, lockfile, package source, build ID and unexpected runtime observations without reinstalling the package to reproduce the alert.
The development platform owner pauses affected release promotion and identifies where release40 has already been consumed.
SOC L1 records build secret access, outbound connections and current runner state. A signed output does not by itself establish trustworthy provenance.
MLOps or application owners check whether the artefact is code, container, model or configuration and identify the relevant approval and signing authority.
The vendor or registry liaison validates the publisher and incident notice through known contacts, keeping local impact separate from supplier claims.
SOC L1 escalates with build b4040, exposed secret references, deployed consumers and pending release actions that require immediate control.

steps: The incident commander appoints development platform, signing, application, endpoint, vendor and identity leads under one release incident.
The release authority defines freeze scope, approved fallback and rollback criteria, including the business effect of removing a widely used update.
The response lead protects clean source repositories, build infrastructure, signing services and recovery artefacts from the affected trust path.

Legal and communications prepare downstream consumer notices based on verified affected versions and digests, with one authorized supplier contact. Authorized activity to test CHG040 approves another dependency and does not authorize the changed publisher or unexpected process.
