steps: Application security traces the exact package version through lockfile, runner b4040, built digest, signing operation, publication and production deployment.
DFIR examines unexpected child processes and network behavior in an isolated analysis environment with appropriate authority, preserving package and runner evidence.
Identity response inventories six accessed build secrets and their downstream permissions, then reviews later use and any derived credentials or sessions.
Development engineering compares source, workflow, branch protection and required reviewers with the last trusted baseline. Preserve approval state and administrative changes.
The signing owner determines which identity signed the release, under what policy and whether the key or authorization path was exposed.
Operations inventories every consumer of affected digests, including cached packages, mirrors, containers and deployments that no longer use the visible tag.
SOC L2 tests CHG040 against the different verified dependency. A legitimate package install or valid signature cannot authorize the unreviewed content.
The supplier liaison requests package provenance, publisher transfer evidence and affected release scope, while local teams retain conflicting or missing evidence explicitly.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The release owner stops affected builds, publication and rollout, quarantining untrusted artefacts and pending promotion jobs after preserving their metadata.
Endpoint response isolates affected runners or management hosts, and identity response revokes exposed CI and deployment credentials at their actual resources.
Registry owners block the specific affected digests and protect mirrors and caches. Record legitimate workloads impacted by the restriction.
Application owners assess each deployed consumer and use a verified clean rollback or compensating restriction with service owner approval.
The signing authority restricts compromised signing paths and starts governed key replacement or certificate actions when exposure warrants them.
SOC verifies no new affected release or credential use after the freeze, including independent deployment routes and supplier update channels. 14 Eradication recovery and closure

Repository owners restore protected review and workflow controls, remove unauthorized tokens or maintainers and correct the proven publisher or pipeline trust failure.
Signing and identity owners replace exposed secrets or keys through their governance process, then update dependent services and verification policy.
Operations replaces affected installed artefacts after validation and retains original package, source and deployment evidence for consumer and incident review.

steps: Application security requires source review, dependency inventory, provenance and independent artefact behavior checks before replacement release approval.

The signing owner confirms expected signatures and release policy enforcement; old compromised credentials or unreviewed workflow paths must fail.
The business owner accepts staged rollout after downstream communications, monitored canary results and a rollback option independent of the affected pipeline.

response_plan.priority_guidance: Declare P1 for imminent material payment diversion or unauthorized privileged reset. A fabricated public statement without critical outage may start at P2.
response_plan.response_lead: Fraud lead with incident commander and communications
response_plan.response_assumption: Treat the urgent executive instruction as a fraud incident and verify whether any associated account, payment or identity reset was compromised. A detector score does not prove synthetic media.

steps: SOC L1 or the service desk preserves the reported call, message or video through an authorized method and records the exact requested action.
Finance pauses the unreleased MYR 280000 instruction and checks actual settlement. The service desk pauses a disputed privileged recovery action.
The executive office verifies the instruction through a known independent channel. Caller ID, a familiar face and fluent speech do not establish authority.
SOC L1 preserves source media, delivery context, message headers and timestamps with restricted access, avoiding unnecessary redistribution of the impersonation.
The identity team checks whether an internal account, privileged session or recovery factor changed during the interaction.
SOC L1 escalates confirmed denial, current business action state, exposed information and the next independent verification needed.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The incident commander assigns fraud, identity response, executive verification, media analysis and communications roles according to the attempted and completed actions.
The authorized business owner freezes high risk instructions connected to the incident while maintaining a verified route for genuine urgent decisions.
Legal and privacy approve recording handling, external reporting and requests to platforms or providers. Retain the original media with evidence custody.

Communications prepares one verified account of service and customer impact, with the official update channel and an assigned next decision time. Authorized activity to test CHG043 includes independent verification and two approvers for a different payment.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: SOC L2 joins the call, follow up email, beneficiary setup and payment queue by time and business identifiers, documenting any uncertain linkage.
Fraud checks earlier instructions, transfers and changed beneficiaries, including actions that completed before the suspicious contact was reported.
Identity response examines privileged recovery, new factors, sessions and directory changes. Validate whether a service desk reset created separate persistent access.
Media specialists examine original provenance and available manipulation indicators without treating an unvalidated score as a conclusive authenticity test.
The executive office records independent denial or approval and the authority scope. Verify the exact amount, recipient or reset rather than a general conversation.
SOC L2 checks official collaboration and public accounts for compromise separately from external impersonation. Lack of takeover does not make the fraudulent instruction legitimate.
Communications scopes fabricated statements, copies, related credential collection sites and actual service load, avoiding unsupported unique viewer counts.
SOC L2 compares CHG043 with its separate verified payment and records missing original media, provider audit and unknown generation method.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Finance maintains holds or initiates recall for settled funds through established bank channels, retaining acknowledgement and reconciliation evidence.
Identity response suspends unsafe recovery and revokes unauthorized sessions or factors while the real account owner is independently verified.
The business owner requires independent callback and dual approval for related high risk requests. Bind any new approval to the exact action and recipient.
Communications issues verified customer or staff instructions through established channels and coordinates impersonation reports or takedowns through authorized owners.
SOC blocks confirmed fraudulent destinations and watches related scams while preserving evidence and legitimate executive or supplier communication.

The incident commander checks whether the impersonation led to any completed action, data disclosure or surviving access; those effects require their own containment. 15 Eradication recovery and closure

The control owner prevents visual or voice familiarity and detector output from serving as sole authorization for sensitive business actions.

steps: Finance reconciles every related transaction and confirms the approved beneficiary and authorization before restarting the workflow.
Identity response tests that the verified owner controls the account and that old unauthorized factors and sessions cannot access privileged services.

The business owner runs a benign impersonation tabletop and accepts normal operations with monitored fraud and service impact triggers.

tool_workflow.label: Cross-tool investigation and resolution
tool_workflow.training_note: Simulated analyst workflow, not a live integration. Product menus, telemetry and response permissions depend on the licensed product version and tenant configuration.
tool_workflow.incident_focus: Deepfake and executive impersonation incidents: Video identity check used to request a privileged reset. Establish confirmed scope, business impact, initial access, affected identities/assets and evidence gaps before selecting disruptive actions.

tools.name: Proofpoint
tools.role: Email security and initial-delivery evidence
tools.investigate: impersonation messages, headers, sender authentication, recipients and campaign scope. Preserve message ID, headers, verdicts, recipients, URLs and attachment hashes where available.
tools.actions: Quarantine/purge only confirmed malicious messages through approved mail-security workflows. Search for campaign-wide recipients and post-delivery exposure.
tools.when_not_applicable: If there is no supported email vector or relevant telemetry, document why Proofpoint is not implicated instead of inventing a finding.

tools.name: CrowdStrike Falcon
tools.role: Endpoint detection, execution and host scope
tools.investigate: endpoint execution only if a user interacted with a link/file; deepfake content alone is not endpoint compromise. Pivot by host/device ID, user, process tree, file hash and UTC event time.
tools.actions: Use approved host containment/remediation only when evidence and incident authority justify it. Record detection/host IDs and action results.
tools.when_not_applicable: If no endpoint is implicated or telemetry is unavailable, document the gap and continue with other relevant sources.

tools.name: ExtraHop
tools.role: Network detection, movement and egress correlation
tools.investigate: network activity only where evidence indicates system access or data transfer. Pivot by source/destination, DNS, protocol, device and UTC time window.
tools.actions: Preserve alert/record identifiers and distinguish observed traffic from inferred intent. Escalate missing visibility as an evidence gap.
tools.when_not_applicable: No observed traffic is not proof of no activity. Record sensor coverage and seek approved alternate telemetry.

tools.name: ServiceNow
tools.role: Incident record, coordination and audit trail
tools.investigate: Create/link the incident and correlate findings from Proofpoint, Falcon and ExtraHop using stable IDs and timestamps. Maintain one authoritative timeline.
tools.actions: Track severity rationale, affected assets/CIs, evidence links, task owners, approvals, communications, containment results, recovery tests and closure sign-off.
tools.when_not_applicable: If ServiceNow is unavailable in the exercise, use a clearly labeled mock ticket rather than implying a real ticket exists.

tool_workflow.correlation_keys: Scenario ID, UTC timestamps, user/principal, host/device ID, source/destination IP, DNS/domain, message ID, URL/file hash, process/detection ID, API/request/session ID where relevant, affected asset/CI and ServiceNow incident number. Use only identifiers relevant to this scenario.
tool_workflow.scenario_specific_check: Use the scenario evidence IDs and UTC timeline to confirm the actual attack path. Record which tools have findings, which are inconclusive, and which are not applicable.
tool_workflow.containment_plan: Pause unverified high-risk transactions through dual-control procedures and verify requests via a trusted known channel.
service_now_fields: Short description with scenario ID and confirmed incident type
Severity and rationale tied to business impact
Affected user, endpoint, application, service or configuration item (CI)
UTC timeline and stable evidence identifiers
Proofpoint, Falcon and ExtraHop findings with evidence links/export references
Facts, hypotheses and evidence gaps clearly separated
Containment/eradication task, owner, approval, timestamp and result
Business impact and privacy/legal/operations escalation where relevant
Recovery tests, residual risk, closure reason and lessons learned
tool_workflow.success_criteria: Verify at the affected resource that the malicious action/access path no longer succeeds, the original cause is addressed, business service functions normally, monitoring shows no recurrence in a defined observation window, and evidence plus residual risks are recorded.
safety_guardrails: Start with read-only investigation where feasible and preserve original evidence and timestamps.
Obtain incident-command, system-owner and change approvals before disruptive actions.
Do not claim a product action succeeded unless its result is recorded and independently verified.
Do not paste passwords, tokens, private keys or unnecessary customer/employee data into ServiceNow.
All timeline events are synthetic training data. Do not execute response actions against production systems.

Legal and privacy approve recording handling, external reporting and requests to platforms or providers. Retain the original media with evidence custody.

steps: Track the video origin and amplified copies without treating repost count as unique viewers. Check whether official accounts were compromised or merely impersonated. Review domains collecting credentials alongside the video.

steps: Communications publishes a verified correction through established channels and coordinates platform reporting. SOC blocks confirmed fraudulent destinations and maintains service capacity monitoring.
phases.source_basis: Scenario-specific response adaptation in the supplied playbook

steps: Remove or report impersonating content through approved legal and platform processes. Repair any confirmed account compromise and improve rapid verification of public statements.
phases.source_basis: Scenario-specific response adaptation in the supplied playbook

steps: Verify customers can locate the official correction and contact center scripts use consistent facts. Monitor continuing copies, fraud reports and service metrics; retain evidence for later requests.
phases.source_basis: Scenario-specific response adaptation in the supplied playbook

steps: Record confirmed actions, affected scope, business impact, and unresolved questions. Separate verified facts from suspected attribution, claimed theft, and unconfirmed impact.

Have the relevant business, privacy, legal, safety, and service owners record impact and notification decisions where applicable.

response_plan.basis: Shared domain response procedure extracted from the supplied playbook.
response_plan.priority_guidance: Declare P1 for confirmed cross tenant sensitive disclosure or destructive tool actions. Unsafe advice without execution may initially be P2.
response_plan.response_lead: AI application owner with privacy and application security
response_plan.response_assumption: Treat assist46 as disclosing confidential tenant B content to tenant A through the retrieval path. Investigate application authorization and downstream execution independently of model behavior.

steps: SOC L1 preserves request q4646, returned response, document IDs and access decisions in restricted evidence storage with unnecessary content excluded from tickets.
The application owner validates tenant A identity and docB46 ownership against authoritative access records, including the explicit deny.
SOC L1 distinguishes retrieval, generated output and actual response delivery. In the sample, response delivery supports confirmed disclosure.
The service owner identifies the deployed application, retrieval index, fallback path and cache versions involved in q4646.
The AI security analyst checks whether tools, scripts or downstream automations consumed the response and could cause additional side effects.
SOC L1 escalates the confirmed disclosure, current unsafe path, known documents and highest priority audit gap to application security and privacy.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The incident commander assigns the AI application owner, application security, retrieval engineering, data ownership, privacy and automation response roles.
The business owner approves disabling the unsafe path or using a bounded read only fallback, recording customer functionality and continuity effects.
The response lead protects original prompts, model and application versions, source documents, tool calls and queue lineage before remedial changes overwrite them.

Privacy and legal begin affected tenant assessment and notification decisions while engineering contains the exposure, using verified facts and stated uncertainty. Authorized activity to test q4600 retrieves an authorized tenant A document and is a valid comparison request.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Application security joins q4646 across authentication, retrieval, citations, response delivery and authorization decisions by stable request and tenant identifiers.
Retrieval engineering inspects semantic fallback, cache keys, index permissions and metadata for missing tenant or object checks.
SOC L2 searches all requests using version 6.1 for mismatched owners, returned document references and recipients, deduplicating actual disclosures.
Data owners verify classification and permissions of retrieved sources. A generated citation or a model assertion is not an authorization grant.
For poisoned knowledge variants, engineering traces source version, contributor identity, ingestion and response use before changing the index.
For unsafe output variants, automation response traces generated text through transformation to the real API or process action and resulting business effect.
SOC L2 validates the approved same tenant request q4600 and tests benign explanation against the exact source, actor, path and result.
DFIR records missing response payloads, expired query logs and unknown human actions. Use isolated synthetic tenants to validate the failed boundary.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: The application owner disables the unsafe retrieval or response path and enforces tenant and object authorization at the service boundary.
Retrieval engineering invalidates affected shared caches and quarantines unauthorized source entries or poisoned versions after preserving provenance.
Automation response stops unsafe execution paths, revokes excessive tool authority and freezes pending side effects that derived from affected responses.
Identity response restricts unauthorized contributor, application or connector credentials and verifies resource level denial independently of the model session.
Privacy and data owners contain sharing of exposed outputs through authorized channels while preserving necessary copies and access records for investigation.

SOC verifies no new cross tenant response, unsafe source citation or unauthorized tool execution. A corrected answer alone does not prove the underlying path is repaired. 16 Eradication recovery and closure
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Application engineering implements deterministic subject, tenant, document and action authorization before retrieval and before delivery or execution.
Retrieval owners rebuild affected indexes, ACL metadata and caches from verified sources, retaining trusted version and provenance references.
Automation engineering validates typed output schemas and allowed operations outside the model, with scoped service identities and approval for sensitive side effects.
Source owners repair knowledge publishing review and contributor access, and engineering adds regression coverage for the actual fallback and cache failure.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: Application security tests allowed and denied cases across two synthetic tenants, normal retrieval, fallback, cache, citation and bulk export paths.
Automation owners test unsafe output rejection and legitimate actions, checking actual destination audit and approval enforcement before tools are restored.
Privacy and data owners reconcile disclosed documents and recipients and review earlier outputs that may have influenced human or automated decisions.
The service owner approves monitored canary operation only after healthy logs, verified data boundaries and a tested shutdown path are available.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: SOC records confirmed disclosure or execution and distinguishes application control failure from hallucination, advice and unverified model compromise claims.
Engineering retains source and application versions, boundary tests and recovery evidence for all affected tenants and downstream action paths.
Privacy and legal record notifications, scope limitations and pending customer reconciliation; assign unresolved log or provider requests to owners.
The incident owner schedules tenant isolation and output handling exercises and tracks root cause changes before final closure.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: SOC L1 captures r5555, input invoice55, the intended task, connector identity, actual beneficiary change and the exact approval record.
Finance holds pay5555 and checks whether money has actually moved. Keep unreleased, settled and recalled instructions distinct.
The orchestration owner identifies running agents, descendants, schedules and durable queues that share agent55 permissions or the affected input.
The connector owner records effective scopes and credential location without copying live tokens into the incident record.
SOC L1 preserves tool parameters, policy decisions, before and after ERP values and destination results, rather than trusting the agent final summary.
SOC L1 escalates the unauthorized side effect, current financial exposure and required stop controls to the incident commander and finance automation owner.

steps: The incident commander assigns finance, orchestration, connector administration, identity, application security and privacy owners according to the reachable business effects.
The business owner approves manual or read only fallback and identifies every sensitive tool that must remain disabled until exact approval enforcement is tested.
The response lead creates a lineage map linking parent and child runs, messages, identities, approvals, connectors, queues and destination actions.

The authorized decision owner records stop authority, rollback limits and reconciliation responsibilities, including actions already delivered that cannot simply be cancelled. Authorized activity to test r5500 is an approved read only summary and does not authorize r5555 writes.
phases.source_basis: Shared response procedure in the supplied playbook

steps: AI security compares the approved summary action with the executed beneficiary parameters and identifies where the service accepted the mismatched approval.
Orchestration response enumerates every run sharing agent55 and all descendants, saved plans, schedules and pending retries using stable task identifiers.
The connector owner checks token exposure, scope, issuing identity and destination audit. A paused runner may coexist with external use of stolen credentials.
Finance reconciles ERP beneficiary changes, payment states, duplicate operations and recipients against authoritative records and independent vendor verification.
For multiagent variants, engineering verifies transport identity, signed task origin, delegated scope and effective worker privilege rather than trusting claimed sender text.
The queue owner distinguishes queued, running, delivered, cancelled and unknown actions and checks idempotency keys, retry budgets and action parameter changes.
AI security tests approved read only run r5500 against its actual scope. Approval for one task cannot authorize later writes, altered recipients or expired actions.

response_plan.bounded_finding: A destructive multi host outage and false public closure claims are confirmed. Their causal linkage and nation state attribution remain unknown. A01 Incident decisions and role authority Use the nearest threat playbook and begin protective action for credible compromise while evidence establishes actual impact. Record confirmed facts, working assumptions and unknowns separately. The priorities below are proposed local defaults requiring organizational approval. Priority Example decision basis Response posture Active destruction critical privilege material sensitive Activate the incident commander and authorized P1 Critical disclosure or financial loss credible safety impact critical emergency response immediately customer outage Confirmed limited compromise exposed credentials or a Assign a qualified response lead and prioritize P2 High contained event with plausible material impact containment by current exposure Blocked or unconfirmed attempt with no demonstrated Validate adjacent paths document the disposition P3 Moderate material effect and reliable controls and monitor for changed impact Verified authorized activity or informational issue Assign an accountable service or detection owner P4 Low requiring routine correction and due date Who acts Role Responsibility SOC L1 Validate the signal preserve identifiers identify immediate harm and escalate with evidence SOC L2 and threat hunting Correlate sources test explanations scope the incident and document coverage limits Incident responder Coordinate technical containment eradication and recovery with the platform owners Acquire and analyze forensic evidence when deeper reconstruction or evidential handling is DFIR needed Incident commander Own cross team priorities decisions communications cadence and accountable closure Platform owner Authorize or execute controls for identity email cloud network applications endpoints or backups Finance fraud OT and facilities Direct financial or physical controls within their specific authority Business privacy legal Accept restored service determine obligations and approve external communications communications Containment can precede full investigation when harm continues. Preserve representative evidence when feasible, record the tradeoff and independently verify the control. A requested action, paused process or console banner is not proof that access or side effects stopped. [R1 R3] A02 Evidence handoff and communication records Preserve before altering when feasible 1 Preserve original records with source system, collector, authority, query or export method, collection UTC, covered interval, original time zone, size and SHA256. Analyze copies with controlled access. 2 Retain source event, observation and ingestion times. Record clock offset, aggregate intervals and missing retention instead of inventing individual timestamps for a summarized count. 3 For transfers, record evidence ID, person releasing and receiving, time, purpose, method and digest verification. A training file checksum does not establish chain of custody for a live incident. 4 Keep live tokens, customer content and untrusted prompts out of broad tickets or external analysis services. Record credential references or digests and restrict the original evidence. 5 Ask DFIR an answerable question and state source availability and business constraints. Do not execute a sample or interrupt a safety process to gather routine evidence. Minimum escalation and situation report Field Record Identification Incident ID reporter service owner current priority and confidence Evidence Confirmed behavior identifiers evidence IDs first and last known times Impact and scope People service data financial and integrity effects confirmed probable and unknown populations Requested versus effective action executor authority verification time business impact expiry and Controls rollback Next decisions Missing evidence named collection owner due time decision owner and next update time zone Recovery Trusted baseline acceptance tests actual reconciliation outstanding risk and business sign off Notification decision record Legal privacy and compliance determine obligations from the current instruments applicable to the entity and event. Record authority and version, applicability, trigger, awareness time, due time and time zone, recipient, approval, submission reference and follow up. Include relevant Malaysian sector policy, personal data duties, NCII designation and contracts where applicable. Do not invent one universal reporting deadline. [R9] Use verified provider and bank contacts. One communications owner issues approved factual updates. Preserve why a notice was required, deferred or not applicable while scope develops. A03 AI agent discovery risk and shutdown Discover actual runtime capabilities through asset records, identity registrations, SaaS and cloud audit, proxy use, notebooks, tool endpoints, schedules and queues. Confirm an accountable owner rather than relying on the product name. Inventory fields Record agent and parent IDs; purpose and business service; owner and alternate; environment; model and application version; autonomy; reachable data classification; retrieval and memory sources; tools and effective permissions; connector credential references; external destinations; approval policy; delegation; queues and schedules; logs and retention; fallback; shutdown method; last stop test; residual risk owner. Local preliminary risk matrix Data reachable Embedded advice Read tools Goal driven actions Multiagent delegation Public Low Low Medium Medium Internal Low Medium Medium High Confidential Medium High High High Restricted High High High High This matrix is an organizational review heuristic, not a probability model. Use actual effective authority. Treat payment, privilege, production execution, safety control, cross tenant read, sensitive export or unverified delegation as High review. Unknown ownership or an untested stop path also requires High review until resolved. Incident priority still follows observed harm. Complete stop and safe restart 1 Preserve input and run lineage, pause new triggers and stop runners and descendants. Verify each acknowledged stop rather than assuming the parent controls every child. 2 Freeze queues and pending side effects after preservation and reconcile running or delivered actions at the destination. Bound retries and prevent duplicate replay. 3 Revoke affected connector credentials at the resource and test old access. Inspect persistent memory and other agents that consumed contaminated inputs. 4 Reconcile business effects and test exact action approval using dummy data. Restart read only with canary users, then restore specific scoped tools after verified logging and a complete stop test. Sensitive approval must bind operation, target, recipient, data, amount where relevant, actor, parameter digest and expiry at the execution service. Text claiming approval is insufficient. [R4 R11] A04 Recovery acceptance and closure checklist 1. Confirm the service is operating from a trusted software, model, configuration and data baseline, with evidence references for each material component. 2. Confirm known persistence and exposed access paths are removed. Test old identities, sessions, keys and approvals at the resource boundary. 3. Verify the entry point and permission defect are fixed or covered by an explicitly accepted temporary control with an owner and expiry. 4. Confirm logging and detection are healthy end to end. Record the searched population, time coverage and any continuing visibility gap. 5. Reconcile data integrity, payment settlement, duplicate actions, restored objects, customer effects and queued work with the relevant business owner. 6. Record notification decisions, submission acknowledgements if applicable and the owner of any pending privacy or legal assessment. 7. Set postrecovery monitoring and escalation triggers. Assign each follow up action a responsible owner, due date and validation evidence. 8. Conduct the review without blame: what failed, why the control permitted it, which signal was missed and which change demonstrably prevents recurrence. 9. Record disposition and confidence. Examples include confirmed incident, prevented attempt, authorized activity or inconclusive due to a named evidence gap. 10. Obtain incident owner and business service acceptance. An open improvement item can transfer to risk treatment; an unresolved active compromise cannot be disguised as an improvement backlog. Suggested metrics: detection to qualified decision; decision to verified containment; service recovery time; actual data loss; confirmed financial loss; evidence collection delay; percentage of affected assets covered; false positive rate by analytic; recurrence; and overdue remediation. Do not improve metrics by changing timestamps, splitting one incident into unlinked tickets or excluding difficult unresolved cases. The pack recovery_acceptance.md and lessons_learned.md provide reusable forms. They include an explicit unresolved items field so the closure record remains honest about scope and residual risk. A05 Reference register Primary sources checked on 19 October 2026. References support the specific principles noted in the text; scenario events, priorities, local procedures and risk scores are original training material. Consult the current full publication and implementation documentation before adopting controls. No attack taxonomy release number is assumed, and no CVE is assigned without verified product applicability. R1 NIST SP 800-61 Revision 3 Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management A CSF 2.0 Community Profile. Final April 2025. Supports integration of response with broader risk management. https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/61/r3/final R2 NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 Framework resource center. Used for Govern Identify Protect Detect Respond and Recover context. https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework R3 Microsoft Learn Revoke user access in Microsoft Entra ID. Explains separate identity tokens and application issued sessions and the need to verify effective revocation. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/users-revoke-access R4 OWASP Gen AI Security Project LLM01 2025 Prompt Injection. Supports treating external content as untrusted and enforcing least privilege and approval for high risk actions. https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/ R5 OWASP API Security Top 10 API1 2023 Broken Object Level Authorization. Supports object level authorization checks for each requested object. https://api-security.owasp.org/editions/2023/en/0xa1-broken-object-level-authorization/ R6 NIST SP 800-82 Revision 3 Guide to Operational Technology Security. Final September 2023. Covers OT reliability performance and safety constraints. Revision 4 was a public draft on the checked date. https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/82/r3/final R7 NIST FIPS 203 Module Lattice Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism Standard ML KEM. Published August 2024. Check the official page for current errata and implementation guidance. https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/203/final R8 NIST FIPS 204 and FIPS 205 Digital signature standards ML DSA and SLH DSA. They are signature schemes rather than data encryption algorithms. https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/204/final R9 NACSA Act 854 information Official overview of the Cyber Security Act 2024 and its NCII related scope. It is a starting point for applicability review rather than a complete notification procedure. https://www.nacsa.gov.my/act854.php R10 UK National Cyber Security Centre Incident management collection. Additional primary operational guidance for preparation response and recovery. https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/incident-management FIPS 205 companion page https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/205/final R11 OWASP Agentic AI Threats and Mitigations Additional threat model background for agent permissions, delegation, memory and tool risks. https://genai.owasp.org/resource/agentic-ai-threats-and-mitigations/ A06 Threat playbook index The document begins directly with a scenario. Every threat has a main scenario, 36 numbered actions and two additional scenarios with evidence and specific response changes. All scenario people, systems, amounts and indicators are fictional. The topic list follows the supplied image; its plotted positions are not used as severity scores. No Threat Main evidence Scenarios 01 Phishing and business email compromise PB001 01A 01B 01C 02 Ransomware and data extortion PB004 02A 02B 02C 03 API attacks and authorization failures PB007 03A 03B 03C 04 Distributed denial of service and resource exhaustion PB010 04A 04B 04C 05 Employee misuse and insider risk PB013 05A 05B 05C 06 Physical intrusion lost devices and removable media PB016 06A 06B 06C 07 Customer account takeover PB019 07A 07B 07C 08 Identity token and privileged access abuse PB023 08A 08B 08C 09 Third party and service provider compromise PB025 09A 09B 09C 10 Internet facing gateway and server compromise PB028 10A 10B 10C 11 Cyber physical and operational technology compromise PB031 11A 11B 11C 12 Quantum related cryptographic exposure PB034 12A 12B 12C 13 AI infrastructure and model platform compromise PB037 13A 13B 13C 14 Software build dependency and update compromise PB040 14A 14B 14C 15 Deepfake and executive impersonation incidents PB043 15A 15B 15C 16 AI application and retrieval compromise PB046 16A 16B 16C 17 Prompt injection and untrusted content instructions PB050 17A 17B 17C 18 AI augmented phishing malware and adaptive campaigns PB053 18A 18B 18C 19 Agentic automation and multiagent hijack PB055 19A 19B 19C 20 Suspected nation state and persistent targeted intrusion PB058 20A 20B 20C Generic labels such as Identity EDR ToolAudit and action names describe normalized simulated observations, not exact vendor schemas. The records may include controls already requested or completed; responders verify their current effect before repeating them. These local playbooks use triage investigation containment eradication recovery and closure for operation. NIST SP 800-61 Revision 3 places incident response within CSF 2.0 risk management; it does not mandate this document numbering. [R1 R2]
